summary: Clarifies how Globally Routable User Agent URIs (GRUUs) should be used with the SIP event notification framework. Experience after RFC 6665 showed that the original text left room for different readings. This document spells out the intended behavior and updates RFC 6665.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7621 clarifies the SIP event framework's requirement to use a Globally Routable User Agent URI (GRUU). It applies to all dialog-forming methods, including INVITE, with an exception for dialogs that reject all subscription requests.

subtitle: Clarifies when SIP notifiers must use a GRUU as their local target.

tldr.problem: Implementers interpreted the GRUU requirement in the SIP event notification framework in different ways, including whether it covered dialogs created by INVITE.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC clarifies that notifiers must use a GRUU for all dialog-forming and target-refresh methods, with a narrow exception for dialogs that reject every subscription request.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7621 updates RFC 6665 with explicit requirements for GRUU handling.

today: RFC 7621 is a Proposed Standard from August 2015 and updates RFC 6665.

sections.title: The Source of Confusion
sections.content:
Experience after publication of the SIP event notification framework in RFC 6665 showed that its instructions for Globally Routable User Agent URIs (GRUUs) could be interpreted in different ways. RFC 7621 clarifies the intended behavior and updates RFC 6665.

The original requirement said notifiers must implement the GRUU extension and use a GRUU as their local target. The clarification explains which dialogs that requirement covers.
sections.plainLanguage: Implementers read the GRUU rule in RFC 6665 differently. This memo states clearly which SIP dialogs must use a GRUU.

sections.title: When a Notifier Must Use a GRUU
sections.content:
Notifiers MUST implement the GRUU extension and use a GRUU as their local target for all dialog-forming methods and all target-refresh methods. This includes dialogs created by INVITE, not only dialogs created by SUBSCRIBE.

The exception is a dialog for which the notifier will reject all subscription requests, whether implicit or explicit. If the notifier uses a non-GRUU local contact under this exception, it MUST reject any SUBSCRIBE or REFER request that might create a subscription. The rejection code SHOULD be 403 (Forbidden), unless another code is more appropriate.
sections.plainLanguage: Use a GRUU for every dialog-forming and target-refresh method, including INVITE. A notifier using the exception must reject every request that could create a subscription.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The RFC says this clarification introduces no security issues beyond those discussed in RFC 6665. It requests no actions from IANA.
sections.plainLanguage: The clarification adds no new security issues, and it requires no IANA changes.
